story.head: Picky vs. trigger-happy
paras: The Bruins won the teams’ first meeting this season, 4-3 in overtime in Winnipeg on Oct 2. The Jets (11-9-3) beat the Islanders 4-3 in overtime on Thursday, and the Bruins (14-7-1) beat Detroit 4-1 on Nov 18. Going in, the Jets are sixth in the Central (tied for 15th in the NHL) and the Bruins fourth in the Atlantic (tied for tenth).
The Jets’ record (.543) is about what their chances are worth. The Bruins’ record (.659) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.584), largely thanks to their goaltending.

The Jets create more chances on the penalty kill than almost anyone (3rd) and rarely ice the puck (5th). The Bruins, by contrast, rarely threaten on the penalty kill (31st). The Jets also get their shots through to the net (4th), and their knack for getting shots through meets a team that blocks a lot. The Bruins leave the shooting to their forwards (lowest) and sit back rather than chase on the forecheck (2nd lowest). Boston has allowed 2.55 goals a game, the fourth fewest in the league. The Bruins wait for good looks, but the Jets settle for hopeful ones.

Mark Scheifele (7 G / 22 A / 29 P in 23 GP) leads the Jets in scoring and is tied for tenth in the NHL, with eleven points in his last five games and four goals in six games against Boston since 2023-24. Kyle Connor (18 G / 10 A / 28 P in 23 GP) has a team-high 18 goals, tied for third in the NHL, with nine points in his last five games. For the Bruins, David Pastrňák (10 G / 18 A / 28 P in 22 GP) leads the way in scoring, with a point in six straight games against Winnipeg.
Stuart Skinner (7-5-3 / .883 SV% in 16 GS) will likely start for Winnipeg, and Jeremy Swayman (10-5-1 / .908 SV% in 16 GS) for Boston.
